The school, which was part of the Trojan Horse scandal inspection, refused admission to over 25 latecomers, including a grandmother who traveled 130 miles from London. The head teacher, Jamie Barry, defended the policy, stating it was to prevent disruption. Parents expressed anger and disappointment, with some citing traffic delays. The school plans to clarify its policy for future events. The concert involved 478 pupils and had limited seating, with the school meeting safeguarding requirements despite past controversies.

article_content: The highly anticipated YSL Forever Light Creator has already garnered significant interest, with thousands of women reserving the product. Going on sale today, this anti-aging cream promises a 'flawless complexion' by utilizing light reflection. Around 15,000 individuals have downloaded vouchers for samples, and over 3,000 have pre-ordered the cream developed by Yves Saint Laurent. The demand is so intense that a helpline has been established for those who find their local pharmacy out of stock. Available as a lotion or serum, the product claims to even out skin tone and eliminate dark spots and shadows. It contains three types of sugars known as glycans, which naturally occur in the skin but decrease with age, leading to a duller and less flexible complexion. The cream is priced between £35 and £82, depending on the bottle size, and is targeted at women over 25. Amandine Ohayon, the general manager of Yves Saint Laurent, described the product as a 'world first,' developed over three years. She noted that current research indicates women are more concerned about age spots and uneven skin tone than wrinkles. The cream is said to improve skin noticeably within a week and reduce red and dark spots within two months. However, experts are skeptical about such claims. Dr. Ross Perry, a cosmetic surgeon, stated that skin tone and pigmentation are subjective and that no cream can completely eliminate blemishes. Dr. Sam Bunting, a cosmetic dermatologist, also expressed doubts about the effectiveness of non-prescription products on red areas caused by sun damage or rosacea.

article_content: On Thursday, Karren Brady, the vice-chairman of West Ham, officially joined the House of Lords. Alongside her was Lord Alan Sugar, a close associate. Brady, now known as Baroness Brady of Knightsbridge, was dressed in traditional red ermine robes as she entered the busy chamber. With Lord Sugar by her side, she pledged her loyalty to the Queen and was warmly applauded by fellow peers. Brady, aged 45 and originally from Birmingham, was one of 22 individuals awarded a Conservative Party Peerage by Prime Minister David Cameron in August. She was escorted by Lord Feldman of Elstree during her introduction as 'Baroness Brady, of Knightsbridge in the City of Westminster'. After the ceremony, she will simply be referred to as Baroness Brady. Following the formalities, Brady signed the House's code of conduct and exchanged greetings with Lord Speaker Baroness D'Souza and the Leader of the House, Baroness Stowell of Beeston. She then left to change out of her ceremonial attire. Previously, Brady had spoken in favor of stay-at-home mothers, emphasizing that their work should not be undervalued. She shared her own experience, admitting that she found staying at home unrewarding during a five-month break from work between 2009 and 2010. Brady, who became the managing director of Birmingham City at 23, praised women who dedicate themselves to their families. 'I had five months where I didn’t work and I found it really unrewarding. All the things you do at home are just taken for granted,' she stated. She highlighted the importance of recognizing the value of stay-at-home mothers. Brady's career includes turning around Birmingham City from near bankruptcy to a valuation of £82 million. In 2013, she played a key role in securing West Ham as the long-term tenant of the Olympic Stadium.

Després de la cerimònia, se la coneixerà simplement com a Baronesa Brady. Després de les formalitats, Brady va signar el codi de conducta de la Cambra i va saludar el Lord Speaker Baronessa D'Souza i el líder de la Cambra, la baronessa Stowell de Beeston. article_content: Newcastle United is reviving its interest in signing Wilfried Zaha from Manchester United. The former Crystal Palace winger had hoped to be part of Louis van Gaal's plans at Old Trafford, but Alan Pardew believes he may be available this summer. Pardew had expressed interest in taking Zaha on loan last January, but the young Englishman moved to Cardiff City instead. Zaha endured a disappointing first season at Old Trafford under David Moyes, where the England under-21 international failed to start a single match in the Premier League before going out on loan. Zaha was Sir Alex Ferguson's final signing as Manchester United manager, joining the club in a £15 million deal and on a five-and-a-half-year contract. The player himself would rather stay in Manchester, with van Gaal's reputation for developing young talent a major attraction, but he is understood to want at least some first-team football.

Zaha va viure una primera temporada decebedora a Old Trafford sota les ordres de David Moyes, on el internacional sub-21 d'Anglaterra no va començar cap partit a la Premier League abans de sortir cedit. article_content: New York (CNN) -- Three defendants pleaded guilty in federal court on Wednesday to conspiring to defraud a Holocaust reparations organization out of $57.3 million, according to court documents. Genrikh Kolontyrskiy, Moysey Kucher, and Dora Kucher, all residents of Brooklyn, were involved in producing and processing thousands of fraudulent applications for the Conference on Jewish Material Claims Against Germany, which is under investigation. The organization, also known as the Claims Conference, distributes over $400 million annually from funds provided by the German government to Holocaust victims. 'Our efforts to hold accountable all individuals who participated in defrauding an organization dedicated to aiding victims of Nazi atrocities continue,' said Preet Bharara, U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of New York, in a statement. The defendants aided in defrauding two funds managed by the Claims Conference: the Article 2 Fund and the Hardship Fund, amounting to $45 million and $12.3 million, respectively, according to court documents. The Article 2 Fund provides monthly payments of around $400 to survivors of Nazi persecution who earn less than $16,000 annually and either lived in hiding or under a false identity for at least 18 months. The Hardship Fund offers a one-time payment of $3,500 to victims of Nazi persecution who were forced to become refugees. Kolontyrskiy, 80, knowingly processed fraudulent applications while employed with the Article 2 Fund. Moysey Kucher, 66, and Dora Kucher, 58, recruited individuals to provide identification documents for fraudulent applications in exchange for money. Jesse Siegel, Kolontyrskiy's attorney, stated that his client was not a major instigator but takes responsibility for his actions. 'He admitted his guilt before the court, and now we hope the judge will put my client's role into context.' Moysey Kucher is extremely remorseful, according to his attorney, Richard Asche. Dora Kucher's attorney, Benjamin Brafman, says Kucher has accepted responsibility for her conduct, which she deeply regrets. 'We are hopeful that at sentencing, the court will find reason to sentence her with great leniency and compassion.' The three defendants were arrested in 2011 and are among 31 people charged with participating in the scheme. To date, 10 former Claims Conference employees have been charged. 'We are grateful to the FBI and U.S. Attorney's Office for their diligent work that resulted in the three guilty pleas,' said Claims Conference public relations manager Amy Wexler in a statement. Kolontyrskiy faces a maximum of 40 years in prison, while Moysey Kucher and Dora Kucher each face a maximum of 20 years in prison. All three defendants are scheduled to be sentenced in August.

Moysey Kucher, de 66 anys, i Dora Kucher, de 58, van reclutar individus per proporcionar documents d'identificació per a sol·licituds fraudulentes a canvi de diners. Jesse Siegel, advocat de Kolontyrskiy, va declarar que el seu client no era un instigador important, però assumeix la responsabilitat de les seves accions. 'Esperem que en el moment de la sentència, el tribunal trobi motius per condemnar-la amb gran indulgència i compassió.' Els tres acusats van ser arrestats el 2011 i són entre 31 persones acusades de participar en l'esquema. Fins ara, s'han presentat càrrecs contra 10 antics empleats de la Conferència de Reclamacions. 'Estem agraïts a l'FBI i a l'Oficina del Fiscal dels Estats Units pel seu treball diligent que va resultar en les tres declaracions de culpabilitat', va dir el gerent de relacions públiques de la Conferència de Reclamacions, Amy Wexler, en un comunicat. Kolontyrskiy s'enfronta a un màxim de 40 anys de presó, mentre que Moysey Kucher i Dora Kucher s'enfronten a un màxim de 20 anys de presó cadascun. Els tres acusats han de ser sentenciats a l'agost.

article_content: Boxing legend Muhammad Ali has been hospitalized again, marking his second admission in just four weeks. Guests at his Scottsdale, Arizona residence discovered him in an unresponsive state, leading to his urgent medical care. The cause is linked to a persistent urinary tract infection that initially sent him to the hospital on December 20. According to family spokesperson Bob Gunnell, Ali is currently stable. Gunnell mentioned that the urinary tract infection remains a concern, necessitating further treatment. A source revealed to Radar Online that Ali had been asleep for an unusually long period, raising alarms among his loved ones. Despite the worries, Ali was discharged on January 6 and celebrated his 73rd birthday with family and friends on January 17. Ali, who has been battling Parkinson's disease since his diagnosis around 1984, has seen a decline in public appearances. However, he still finds joy in social activities and sports. His daughter, Rasheda Ali-Walsh, expressed gratitude for her father's strength and resilience. In recent months, Ali has been treated at a hospital in Kentucky and made a public appearance in Louisville for the Muhammad Ali Humanitarian Awards, where he was honored alongside figures like Jim Brown. Ali and his wife, Lonnie, maintain residences in Paradise Valley, Arizona; Berrien Springs, Michigan; and Louisville, Kentucky.

article_content: Google recently laid off workers in its news unit as the Israel-Hamas conflict continues and disinformation spreads online, according to a report by CNBC on Wednesday. The tech giant let go of an estimated 40 to 45 workers at Google News, as reported by the Alphabet Workers Union to CNBC. The union represents employees at the company. A Google spokesperson confirmed the cuts but did not specify the exact number of jobs affected. Neither Google nor the Alphabet Workers Union responded immediately to Insider's request for comment. Google News is a news aggregation service that compiles information from thousands of global news sources. It allows readers to stay updated on popular stories and global events. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu declared a state of war on October 7 following a surprise attack by Hamas, which launched thousands of rockets into southern and central Israel, resulting in over 1,400 deaths. In response, Israeli retaliatory attacks in Gaza have caused around 3,000 fatalities, according to local authorities. The conflict has seen a surge in misinformation and disinformation online and on social media. Shayan Sardarizadeh, a journalist at BBC Verify, highlighted some of the worst examples on X, formerly known as Twitter. One example included a video falsely claiming to show a Hamas militant air assault on Israel, which was actually footage from the video game Arma 3. Lawmakers are seeking answers from tech giants about the spread of false information. US Senator Michael Bennet sent a letter to the chiefs of Meta, TikTok, X, and Google this week, inquiring about their efforts to tackle this issue. He wrote: 'Deceptive content has spread rapidly across social media sites since the conflict began, often receiving millions of views.' 'In many cases, your platforms' algorithms have amplified this content, contributing to a dangerous cycle of outrage, engagement, and redistribution,' he added. Google CEO Sundar Pichai sent a note to employees on Tuesday regarding the company's efforts to counter disinformation, stating: 'Content moderation on our platforms is a critical focus right now. We will continue to tackle disinformation, hate speech, graphic content, and terrorist content.' However, he did not provide specific details on how the company is addressing these issues. According to The Information, Google has also recently laid off workers in other departments, such as its self-driving car unit, Waymo. This follows substantial layoffs earlier this year, where the tech giant reduced around 6% of its workforce to cut costs.

El gegant tecnològic va acomiadar una estimació de 40 a 45 treballadors a Google News, segons el sindicat Alphabet Workers Union a CNBC. El sindicat representa els treballadors de l'empresa. Un portaveu de Google va confirmar els acomiadaments però no va especificar el nombre exacte de llocs de treball afectats. Ni Google ni el sindicat Alphabet Workers Union van respondre immediatament a la sol·licitud de comentaris d'Insider. Google News és un servei d'agregació de notícies que compila informació de milers de fonts de notícies globals. Permet als lectors mantenir-se actualitzats sobre les històries populars i els esdeveniments mundials. El primer ministre israelià Benjamin Netanyahu va declarar l'estat de guerra el 7 d'octubre després d'un atac sorpresa de Hamàs, que va llançar milers de coets al sud i centre d'Israel, causant més de 1.400 morts. En resposta, els atacs de represàlia israelians a Gaza han causat al voltant de 3.000 morts, segons les autoritats locals. El conflicte ha vist un augment de la desinformació i la desinformació en línia i a les xarxes socials. Shayan Sardarizadeh, periodista de BBC Verify, va destacar alguns dels pitjors exemples a X, abans conegut com a Twitter. Un exemple incloïa un vídeo que afirmava falsament mostrar un assalt aeri de militants de Hamàs a Israel, que en realitat eren imatges del videojoc Arma 3. Els legisladors estan buscant respostes dels gegants tecnològics sobre la propagació d'informació falsa. El senador nord-americà Michael Bennet va enviar una carta als caps de Meta, TikTok, X i Google aquesta setmana, preguntant sobre els seus esforços per abordar aquest tema. Va escriure: 'El contingut enganyós s'ha estès ràpidament pels llocs de xarxes socials des que va començar el conflicte, sovint rebent milions de visualitzacions.' 'En molts casos, els algorismes de les vostres plataformes han amplificat aquest contingut, contribuint a un cicle perillós d'indignació, participació i redistribució', va afegir. El CEO de Google, Sundar Pichai, va enviar una nota als empleats el dimarts sobre els esforços de l'empresa per contrarestar la desinformació, afirmant: 'La moderació de continguts a les nostres plataformes és un focus crític ara mateix. Continuarem abordant la desinformació, l'odi. discurs, contingut gràfic i contingut terrorista.' No obstant això, no va proporcionar detalls específics sobre com l'empresa està abordant aquests problemes. Segons The Information, Google també ha acomiadat recentment treballadors d'altres departaments, com la seva unitat de cotxes autònoms, Waymo. Això segueix acomiadaments substancials a principis d'aquest any, on el gegant tecnològic va reduir aproximadament el 6% de la seva plantilla per reduir costos.
